newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senator says agency favors Pataki contributors.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senator says agency favors Pataki contributors.

text.p: A New York State senator charged that a state agency funneled millions of dollars of grants and loans to 25 firms that gave campaign funds to Gov. George Pataki and U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato.

While nine of the firms gave money to the Pataki Inaugural Committee, the Empire State Development Corp awarded at least 11 contracts to firms that have political links to Pataki, D'Amato, or the state Republican party, his report said.

The report was released on Wednesday by Franz Leichter, D-Manhattan, who last month charged that the state agency was awarding a disproportionate share of its contracts to companies located upstate, at the expense of New York City.

While he also criticized the former Cuomo Adminstration for using the Urban Development Corp, which preceded the Empire State Development, to reward firms for their support, he said the Pataki Administration had worsened the abuses.
Leichter said the head of the Empire State Development, Charles Gargano, had raised $14.5 million for Pataki's 1994 election, adding he also had raised money for D'Amato and the Republican Party.

"It appears that Empire State Development considers a campaign contribution to Pataki as the equivalent of an application for an economic development grant," the state senator said, in prepared remarks.
A spokesman for Pataki referred a call for comment to Gargano, the head of Empire State Development.

Gargano, who released his response through a spokeswoman, reacted angrily to the criticism, saying statistics from the U.S. Bureau of Labor showed the Pataki Administration created more than 100,000 private sector jobs since taking office. He added that unepmployment has fallen to 6 percent since January 1995.

"If Franz Leichter can't get these two basic facts straight -- it's obvious this is pure partisan politics, and it's truly sad that this tax and spend liberal is not interested in creating real jobs for New Yorkers."

A spokesman for D'Amato released the senator's reaction, which also pointed to the creation of more than 100,000 private jobs under the Pataki Adminisration. "That speaks for itself. If talented people are being brought to help bring about this success then I applaud them."

Leichter, noting Chemical Banking Corp and Chase Manhattan gave the Republican Party $55,000 two days after the Pataki Administration approved their merger, said this raised questions about whether companies believe such gifts incline the state to rule in their favor.
Urging that the control of Empire State Development be given to the legislature, the state senator asked Gargano and Pataki to insulate themselves from the grant process.
The New York senator also called upon the legislature to pass a bill he introduced that would bar all state officials from any form of fundraising.
